name: G01 gridPlainBorder: the first character must be a dash
why: no border starts with a plus sign any more, and `-+` is no border either way: the enumerations and the stated rows see it

name: G02 gridPlainBorder: the first-character test inverted
why: a border answers false and a line that does not begin with a plus sign is read as one

name: G03 gridPlainBorder: the first character is not asked
why: `=-+` or `x-+` reads as a border: the wide enumeration holds `=` and `x`, the seeded lines hold `=` and `x`

name: G04 gridPlainBorder: a vertical bar also opens a border
why: `|-+` is a border: no enumeration alphabet holds a bar, the code-unit sweep replaces the first character of `+-+` by every code unit and the seeded pieces hold `|`

name: G05 gridPlainBorder: the walk starts at 0
why: the plus sign is not a dash: no cell is read and every line answers false

name: G07 gridPlainBorder: one cell at most (outer while is an if)
why: `+-+-+` stops after its first cell and the rest of the line is not blank

name: G08 gridPlainBorder: one dash at most in a cell (inner while is an if)
why: `+--+` is read as a dash and then a dash that no plus sign closes

name: G09 gridPlainBorder: the outer loop looks for a plus sign
why: no cell is ever entered: every line answers false

name: G10 gridPlainBorder: the inner loop eats plus signs instead of dashes
why: a cell with a dash in it is not closed any more

name: G11 gridPlainBorder: the inner loop eats everything up to a dash code
why: the dash run swallows the plus sign that closes it (and blanks), so `+-+` fails its closer

name: G12 gridPlainBorder: the inner loop eats any character that is not a plus sign
why: `+-x+` and `+-=+` are borders (the wide enumeration holds `=` and `x`)

name: G14 gridPlainBorder: the closer is not asked
why: `+-x` and `+-=` read as borders: the character that should close the cell is stepped over

name: G15 gridPlainBorder: a vertical bar also closes a cell
why: `+-|` is a border: no enumeration alphabet holds a bar, the sweep puts every code unit in place of the closing plus sign and the seeded pieces hold `|`

name: G16 gridPlainBorder: an equals sign also closes a cell
why: `+-=` is a border: the wide enumeration holds `=`

name: G18 gridPlainBorder: the outer loop also enters on an equals sign
why: equivalent: on an `=` the inner loop reads no dash and the closer test refuses it, so the call answers false where the original left the loop and found the `=` where blanks must be (also false); looked at by hand and against the old pattern on the wide enumeration, which holds `=`

name: G19 gridPlainBorder: the cell count goes up by two
why: equivalent: the count is only compared with 0

name: G20 gridPlainBorder: the cell count goes down
why: a border has a negative count and answers false

name: G21 gridPlainBorder: the cell count never goes up
why: every border has no cell and answers false

name: G22 gridPlainBorder: the count starts at 1
why: a lone plus sign, or a plus sign and blanks, is a border

name: G23 gridPlainBorder: the count is not asked
why: a lone plus sign, or a plus sign and blanks, is a border

name: G24 gridPlainBorder: two cells at least
why: `+-+` has one cell

name: G26 gridPlainBorder: the closing plus sign is not stepped over
why: the walk stays on the plus sign, which is not a blank, so every border answers false

name: G27 gridPlainBorder: the end test inverted
why: a border with nothing after it answers false and a border with text after it answers true

name: G28 gridPlainBorder: the end is reached or passed
why: equivalent: skipBlanks stops at the first character that is not a space or a tab and at the end of the string, so it never answers past the length

name: G29 gridPlainBorder: no blank is allowed after the last cell
why: `+-+ ` and `+-+\t` are borders (the stated rows, the blank enumeration)

name: G30 gridPlainBorder: one character after the last cell is skipped
why: `+-+x` is a border

name: G31 gridPlainBorder: the blanks are skipped from the closing plus sign
why: the plus sign is no blank, so every border answers false

name: G32 gridPlainBorder: any white space may end the line (trim)
why: `+-+\n`, a no-break space, a form feed and U+2028 after the last cell are blanks (the stated rows, the wide enumeration holds `\n` and the no-break space)

name: G34 gridPlainBorder: spaces only after the last cell
why: `+-+\t` is not a border

name: G36 gridPlainBorder: the first character is read as a string
why: equivalent: the character at 0 is the plus sign in both spellings, and an empty line gives NaN in the first and undefined in the second, both different from the plus sign

name: G37 gridPlainBorder: a dash run is read to 65,535 characters
why: `+` and 100,000 dashes and `+` is a border (the dash-run rows hold 1,000, 100,000 and 1,000,000)

name: G38 gridPlainBorder: 4,096 cells at most
why: the 65,536-cell and 1,000,000-cell rows answer false

name: G39 gridPlainBorder: 1,048,576 cells at most
why: the 3,000,000-cell row answers false

name: G40 gridPlainBorder: 4,194,304 cells at most
why: the 6,800,000-cell rows (the document rows and the oracle) answer false

name: G41 gridPlainBorder: 16,777,216 cells at most
why: the 20,000,000-cell linear-time row answers false (the 12,000,000-cell row is below the cap)

name: G42 gridPlainBorder: a line of 8,388,608 characters at most
why: every document row of 13.6 million characters answers false, the rows' stated headings change

name: C01 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the loop stops at a line that is a border
from: while (k < x && !gridPlainBorder(lines[k])) {
to: while (k < x && gridPlainBorder(lines[k])) {
why: the table is taken to begin at the wrong line, or not at all: the grid-table rows of qmd-model.test.ts, the line-block rows and the markdown-hint document rows

name: C02 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the loop looks at the last line only
from: while (k < x && !gridPlainBorder(lines[k])) {
to: while (k < x && !gridPlainBorder(lines[x])) {
why: a line block above the border is not skipped (the rows with a `| lb` line above the border)

name: C03 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the loop runs one line further
from: while (k < x && !gridPlainBorder(lines[k])) {
to: while (k <= x && !gridPlainBorder(lines[k])) {
why: a first guess of equivalence was wrong: with no border in the run the loop ends one line past it, and when that line is a border `startsAtBoundary(b, k)` asks this function for the line above again, an unbounded recursion (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded, found by the random corpus); a document with a border directly under a run that holds none

name: C04 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the loop never advances
from: while (k < x && !gridPlainBorder(lines[k])) {
to: while (false) {
why: a line block above the border is not skipped, so the table begins at the line block

name: C05 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the border of the run is not asked
from: if (gridPlainBorder(lines[k]) && startsAtBoundary(b, k)) {
to: if (startsAtBoundary(b, k)) {
why: equivalent: the loop above leaves k on a border (k < x) or on x; on x the borders loop counts at most one line, and one border is not two, so the answer is false whether or not the test runs; the lone-border document rows exist to reach THIS call and throw if it were a pattern again

name: C06 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the border of the run or the boundary
from: if (gridPlainBorder(lines[k]) && startsAtBoundary(b, k)) {
to: if (gridPlainBorder(lines[k]) || startsAtBoundary(b, k)) {
why: a first guess of equivalence was wrong: a plain border no longer needs a block boundary above it, so a table that begins under a paragraph line ends a block (killed by the same older row of qmd-model.test.ts as C07; the two new files alone do not kill it)

name: C07 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the boundary is not asked
from: if (gridPlainBorder(lines[k]) && startsAtBoundary(b, k)) {
to: if (gridPlainBorder(lines[k])) {
why: a table whose first border is not at a block boundary (`+-+` directly under a paragraph line) ends a block: killed by one older row of qmd-model.test.ts, `MUTATION KILLER: a grid table directly under a raw TeX environment` (the two new files alone do NOT kill it: measured by hand, 0 failed of 92)

name: C08 tableOrLineBlockEndsAt: the border call is negated
from: if (gridPlainBorder(lines[k]) && startsAtBoundary(b, k)) {
to: if (!gridPlainBorder(lines[k]) && startsAtBoundary(b, k)) {
why: a table whose first border is a plain border answers false (the markdown-hint document rows with a `## In` inside the opener, and the grid-table rows of qmd-model.test.ts)
